comparator.name: Cognition, Language and Communication
comparator.sourceNotes: The 2026–2027 regulations specify a 150 EC common structure including free electives, and 30 EC in the Psychology specialisation. The example uses the required Brain & Cognition course, all three B&C options and one Current Topics course. Cognitive Modelling is counted once.
components: Leading Questions in Cognition, Language and Communication
Designing Research in Cognition, Language and Communication
Computational Perspectives on Cognition and Language
Philosophy of the Humanities (Language and Cognition)
Cognition, Language and Communication in Research Papers
Introductory Psychology and Brain & Cognition – part B: Brain & Cognition
Beyond Speech: Language and Cognition across Modalities
Current Topics: Consciousness: From Theory to the Clinic

core: Cognition, language and communication studied together across humanities, behavioural science and computational science
Empirical inquiry using experimental, qualitative, statistical and computational methods
A disciplinary specialisation, open elective space and a culminating bachelor research project
adjacent: Artificial intelligence, programming and cognitive modelling
Linguistics, psycholinguistics and language learning and use
Communication science, rhetoric, persuasion, social interaction and multimodality
Philosophy, Dutch language and literature, music and cultural expression
questions: How do brain and mind make language, memory, attention and reasoning possible?
How can computational models and artificial intelligence explain or shape cognition and language?
How do rhetoric, persuasion, interaction and communication channels shape mutual understanding?

candidates.label: Language & Communication Studies
candidates.reason: These directions already form the defining language-and-communication spine of the closest match rather than a separate remaining alternative.

candidates.label: Philosophy of Mind & Language
candidates.reason: Coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included.

candidates.label: Music, Cognition & Culture
candidates.reason: Coherent direction, but three alternatives are already included.

alternatives.label: Language, cognition and communication
alternatives.labelReason: Combines empirical language, cognition and persuasion with stylistic and media analysis.
alternatives.concept: Studies how people process language, interpret messages and respond to persuasion. Research methods and courses in psychology, rhetoric and media connect these questions to experiments, texts and communication in practice.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics. Statistics and Experimental Methods precedes advanced evidence synthesis. Rhetoric precedes advanced persuasion and communication projects.

alternatives.label: Cognitive psychology and neuroscience
alternatives.concept: Studies the neural bases of behaviour, perception, memory and language, alongside development and mental health. Experimental statistics and research synthesis support the study of behaviour.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative replaces most communication, language and humanities breadth with a sustained psychology, neuroscience, life-science and biomedical sequence.
progression: Brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics. Cell biology precedes molecular laboratory work and introductory experimental methods precede meta-analysis.
alternatives.labelReason: Develops empirical cognition and neuroscience with supporting life science and psychology.

alternatives.label: Computation and cognitive science
alternatives.labelReason: Builds computational and statistical tools and applies them alongside empirical cognition and language study.
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, algorithms and machine learning with the study of language and cognition. It develops mathematical tools for modelling and uses psychology and ethics to examine how people think and interact with AI.
progression: Programming and mathematical methods precede advanced algorithms, deep learning and optimisation. Brain and behaviour precedes Psycholinguistics.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest pathway, this alternative replaces most society, media, literature and qualitative breadth with a continuous programming, data, mathematics and artificial-intelligence spine.

blocks: The UCR computation option develops programming and modelling. The UvA course applies computational perspectives directly to cognition and language.
Logic, probability and computational methods provide related tools. UvA applies formal language theory and information theory to language questions.
UCR uses models in data science and AI. UvA uses computational models to test theories of human cognition.
Both examine philosophical questions about mind and cognition. UvA connects these questions to research in language and the humanities.
Both develop neuroscience foundations. UCR includes comparative nervous systems and behaviour.
Both investigate perception through cognitive neuroscience. UvA follows perception into the study of consciousness.
Both study language processing through cognitive neuroscience. UvA also gives dedicated attention to memory and emotion.
Both introduce relationships between brain and behaviour. UvA’s course is the gateway to the Psychology electives.
Both address the relation between social interaction and cognition. UvA emphasises qualitative analysis of interaction.
Both apply statistics in R to empirical questions. UCR focuses on experimental and behavioural research.
Both develop advanced quantitative research skills. UCR focuses on systematic review and meta-analysis.
Selected courses address individual topics in cognition, language and communication. UvA introduces them together through research questions.
UCR studies mind and language in psycholinguistics and philosophy. UvA makes their relationship the central topic of a separate course.
UCR studies cognition, consciousness and mental health in separate courses. UvA connects consciousness research to clinical questions in one course.
Both study rhetoric and argumentation. UvA also covers speech-act theory.
Both examine how people are persuaded. UCR applies its tools in a community communication project.
Both address communication beyond words. UCR uses creative work in sound, voice and performance. UvA studies communication across modalities through cognitive and linguistic research.
UCR offers psycholinguistics and stylistic analysis. Neither serves as a broad introduction to linguistic structure.
UCR experimental statistics and qualitative methods develop related skills. This UvA course integrates them in CLC research design.
UCR courses use research projects in their own subjects. UvA requires a first-year research project in CLC.
Selected courses use research articles. UvA dedicates a course to critically connecting studies across the field.
Selected UCR courses include empirical research. UvA has a required second-year project that builds on the common sequence.
Some UCR courses involve community projects. UvA requires a dedicated application project with an external partner.
The UvA thesis is required. UCR independent research is optional and appears separately.
This is open elective space rather than a specific course.

routeSelection.basis: Psychology is the first specialisation named in the official public explanation. The example uses the three Brain & Cognition electives and the first-listed Current Topics elective in the adopted regulation. Course choice and year placement follow CLC-specific entry rules and the current offering periods.

selection.assessment: The closest option combines language processing, social cognition, persuasion and empirical research. The cognitive psychology option deepens brain and behaviour. The computational option develops algorithmic and mathematical approaches with a cognition strand. These have distinct advanced work and satisfy the three-option limit. Further language, philosophy and music directions were considered. Their relevant content either supports the closest option or lacks the depth for an additional composition.

notes.text: UvA combines linguistics, cognition and communication with a linked research sequence and a required thesis. UCR offers related courses in psycholinguistics, neuroscience, communication and computation. Its linguistics training and research sequence differ from those at UvA.

audience.programmeDescription: Cognition, Language and Communication at the University of Amsterdam studies how people think, use language and communicate. Students learn to investigate these questions and choose a specialisation. This example follows Psychology.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option connects language processing, cognition and persuasion. Two related options give more weight to neuroscience or computation.

componentNotes.uva-58413: The example places Cognitive Modelling in year two and counts it once.
componentNotes.uva-57795: The required thesis follows the core courses and Advanced Statistics.
componentNotes.y3-free: The regulations allow the 30 EC of free electives across years two and three. This example places them in year three.
